newsitem.title: UK: Eastbound dirty tankers firm for forward dates.
newsitem.headline: Eastbound dirty tankers firm for forward dates.

text.p: World crude tanker rates stayed firm for forward loadings but despite weaker levels for prompt loading on Tuesday, brokers said.
Mideast/Japan was again fixed at W75 for 250,000 tonnes, the same level as on Monday. But brokers said prompt loadings talked nearer W60 to W65.
Sailings to Singapore from the Mideast Gulf confirmed the firm tone going east after Shell fixed the Berge Bonde at W60, the same as Monday's level and above last week's W54.
Despite the gains refinery profit margins have sagged in Singapore and may curb crude demand over the next few days, oil traders said.
In the West the Mediterranean market held steady at W120 for 80,000 tonnes but the market for 130,000 tonne vessels was described by one broker as "on its knees" and talking around W80.
West African rates held steady again while rates from the North Sea to the U.S. continued to fall.
Independent trader and refiner Vitol paid W115 for an Aframax to the U.S. while Texaco paid the same rate to Pembroke, compared to W110 on Monday.
